title: Access review audit timeline and evidence heuristics — 2026 Q1
body:
Purpose:
This working note captures the audit timeline, pragmatic heuristics for evidence collection, and SIEM export considerations for quarterly least-privilege recertification and privileged access audits. Intended audience: S&C engineers, SRE partners, product owners running Dedicated/Private, and compliance reviewers.

Background and motivation:
We are moving from a largely manual quarterly recertification to a hybrid model that combines RBAC v2 role snapshots, deterministic evidence artifacts, and lightweight sampling to reduce reviewer burden while preserving audit quality. This doc records lessons from the Jan 2026 pilot (teams: infra, private-deployments, serving-runtime) and proposes heuristics and concrete SIEM/audit-log fields to make evidence automation repeatable.

Summary of pilot outcomes (Jan 2026):
- Scope: 470 principals (users+service accounts) across 6 sensitive roles (k8s-admin, infra-prod-deploy, kms-admin, db-admin, ci-runner, support-impersonate).
- Manual review time reduced from estimated 40h to 11h using automated evidence pre-collection + sampled confirmations.
- Two gaps found: 1) stale service-account tokens issued by legacy CI; 2) role bindings with broad namespace '*'. Both remediated within sprint.

Audit timeline (recommended cadence & milestones):
- T-28 days: Generate RBAC v2 role snapshot export (roles + bindings + role-hierarchy, immutable snapshot id). Flag any bindings containing wildcard resources.
- T-21 days: Run evidence automation pipelines to attach artifacts to each principal: last-login, active-sessions, recent-token-issuance, last-justification (if workflow used), config-change diff.
- T-14 days: Initial reviewer package created: CSV + evidence links per principal + risk score (automated). Assign reviewers and sample sets.
- T-7 days: Reviewer feedback due; automated follow-ups for principals with no justification.
- T-0 days: Recertification decision recorded (approve/approve-with-constraints/revoke). Export final attestation bundle to SIEM/s3 for retention.

Heuristics for what counts as "sufficient evidence":
(These are intentionally pragmatic; goal is high signal-to-noise for auditors)
1) Human user — low activity (no login > 90d): require either justification link OR manager attestation captured in ticket.
2) Service account — no invocation in 60d: require recent deploy pipeline run evidence OR a config entry showing it was used for long-running job.
3) Admin-role assignments created < 30d: require change-ticket id and approving manager in audit log; otherwise escalate.
4) Role with wildcard resources: treat as high-risk; require direct owner and a justification note in the attestation flow.
5) Temporary elevations (just-in-time): must have correlated audit_log entries showing start/end times and justification id.

Minimum evidence artifacts (what automation should attach):
- rbac_snapshot_id: unique export id for the RBAC v2 snapshot
- role_snapshot_csv: flattened roles+bindings for reviewer download
- last_auth: timestamp of last successful auth (user or SA)
- token_issue_events: list of token creation events (limited to 90d) as links to SIEM search URIs
- active_sessions_count: integer from session-store export
- related_prs/issues: Slack thread / PR / ticket link used to request the role
- config_diff: diff showing when binding was created/changed and by whom
- justification_url: link to Attestation workflow item (if present)

Audit log schema recommendations (fields we should standardize across services):
- event_id (string) — UUID
- ts (iso8601)
- actor_principal (string) — user or service account id; include type prefix (user: /sa: )
- actor_type (string) — human|service|robot|external
- action (string) — e.g., role.bind, role.unbind, auth.success, auth.fail, token.issue, token.revoke, iam.impersonate
- target_resource (string) — canonical resource path (k8s:/cluster/ns/name, aws:/arn, rdb:/db/schema)
- role_snapshot_id (string) — if event caused a snapshot change reference
- justification_id (string) — if a justification workflow was used
- request_id (string) — correlation id across frontend/backend
- session_id (string) — ephemeral session or token id
- ip_address (string)
- user_agent (string)
- change_set_url (string) — link to config change (git/PR)
- raw_payload (string) — compressed/minified JSON of original event for debugging

SIEM export considerations and sample queries:
- Exports should be stored by snapshot id and day (s3://redwood-audit/2026-01/rbac_snapshot_<id>), with an index file that maps snapshot->ticket attachments.
- Provide pre-built Kibana/Splunk queries: e.g.
  * Find recent wildcards: action:role.bind AND target_resource:"*" | table actor_principal, ts, change_set_url
  * Token churn: action:token.issue earliest=-90d | stats count by actor_principal | where count>5
  * JIT elevation mismatches: action:iam.impersonate AND NOT justification_id exists | table actor_principal, ts, target_resource

Sample Elastic query (approx):
  GET /_search
  {
    "query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"action": "role.bind"}}, {"match_phrase": {"target_resource": "*"}}]}}
  }

Evidence retention & export policy:
- Attestation bundles + raw logs for recertification must be retained for 3 years. Daily-indexed SIEM exports are the canonical chain-of-evidence.
- Snapshots are immutable; any re-export must reference original snapshot id and record the reason.

RBAC v2-specific notes and pitfalls observed:
- Role aliasing: teams often create local role aliases that map back to global roles. Snapshot export must resolve aliases to canonical role ids to avoid duplicate reviewer workload.
- Bindings with multiple principals (CSV in single binding): flatten to per-principal records in the reviewer package so reviewers can act per principal.
- Managed vs ephemeral keys: mark service accounts with key rotation metadata (last-rotated, reuse-count) as extra evidence.

Sampling strategy for reviewers (keeps workload manageable):
- Always include 100% of principals in high-risk roles.
- Include 25% random sample from medium-risk roles + 10% from low-risk roles.
- Add all principals with anomalies (multiple tokens in last 7d, wildcard resources, no manager on file).
- Rotating sample: ensure 100% coverage over 4 quarters by rotating which low-risk principals are sampled.

Action items from pilot (owners + due dates):
- Evan Li: implement role alias resolution in export pipeline (due 2026-02-12)
- Aisha Kaur: add justification_url field to attestation workflow and wire into reviewer package (due 2026-02-05)
- Diego Martinez: create SIEM export index file format and S3 lifecycle policy (due 2026-02-19)
- Priya Nandan: update ops-runbook for recertification T-28 -> T-0 timeline and share with Product Ops (due 2026-02-01)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How strict should the automation be about requiring tickets for changes <30d? (Tradeoff: velocity vs auditability)
- Retention costs vs auditor preference for raw payload access — propose raw payload retrieval on-demand after 30d (cold storage).
- Integration with Dedicated customer-managed KMS audit streams: should they be mirrored into Redwood SIEM index or referenced externally?

Appendix: quick checklists for automation engineers
- Export: ensure rbac_snapshot_id in filename and top-level json property.
- Evidence attach: link token_issue_events back to SIEM saved-search URI rather than embedding full event lists.
- SIEM: include index templates that map event_id, ts, actor_type, action as keyword fields to speed queries.
- Reviewer package: csv columns = principal_id, principal_type, roles_csv, last_auth, active_sessions_count, risk_score, evidence_links

Notes to reviewers (how to use this package):
- Start with risk_score > 7; inspect evidence_links -> config_diff and token_issue_events first.
- For service accounts: prefer concrete invocation evidence (pipeline run, cron entry) over manager attestations.
- When revoking an account, include remediation steps in ticket: rotate keys, remove bindings, invalidate sessions.

This is a working doc. Add comments inline where you see gaps. We will incorporate feedback and produce a finalized runbook (expected Q1 release).

Document history:
- 2026-01-15: initial draft by PN

- 2026-02-02: added SIEM query examples and action items (Aisha)
